xBRIEFInfo.description: Scope xBRIEF ingested from GitHub issue #2064

plan.title: consolidate: redirect deft install-upgrade to directive update (Option A)

narratives.Description: Operators have two overlapping upgrade-adjacent verbs (deft install-upgrade and directive update). Consolidate to a single mental model by making install-upgrade a thin redirect that delegates to the update path with a one-line notice and no behavioral drift.
narratives.UserStory: As a consumer upgrading a vendored install, I want deft install-upgrade to delegate to directive update (single upgrade path: npm i -g -> deft update -> deft migrate -> deft doctor), so I do not have to reason about two upgrade-adjacent commands with overlapping semantics.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. Implement Option A (redirect) -- the recommended path in the issue. Locate the current TS surfaces: the install-upgrade command (packages/cli/src/install-upgrade* / packages/core install-upgrade path) and the update command (directive update / runRefreshDeposit). 2. Make install-upgrade print a one-line deprecation/redirect notice and delegate to the SAME code path as directive update (share runRefreshDeposit or call update directly) so output + effects are identical. 3. Preserve any genuinely install-upgrade-only side effect if one exists (marker/manifest write) -- verify-first whether install-upgrade does anything update does not; if it does and it is still needed, fold it into the shared path rather than dropping it. Do NOT regress #2053 version resolution or #2055/#2056 refresh transaction. 4. Parity tests: on a vendored install fixture, install-upgrade and directive update produce identical deposit state / output; the redirect notice is emitted. 5. Update UPGRADING.md + doctor signpost prose to name the single canonical verb. 6. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry. 7. Run repo-root pnpm run lint (full-file lane) + task check. If verify-first reveals install-upgrade has a load-bearing behavior that CANNOT be safely folded into update (making Option A unsafe), STOP-AND-REPORT with the finding and a recommendation for Option B (documented dual surface) instead of half-redirecting.
narratives.Overview: See https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/2064. Umbrella #2057 closed after behavioral fixes (#2058) + discoverability (#2062); both verbs work on vendored installs but overlap. Option A: install-upgrade -> thin redirect to directive update with parity. Option B (fallback): document dual surface. Default to A unless verify-first shows a redirect would drop a needed behavior.
narratives.GuardRails: TS-native repo. Legacy Go installer is FROZEN (verify:go-freeze) -- do NOT modify Go installer code; fix the TS update/install-upgrade path only. Prefer Option A (redirect). Prove parity with tests on a vendored-install fixture. Preserve #2053/#2055/#2056 guarantees. If Option A is unsafe, stop and report rather than shipping a partial redirect.

items.title: Decision implemented: install-upgrade redirects to directive update (Option A) unless verify-first proves it unsafe (then stop-and-report for Option B).
install-upgrade delegates to the update path with a one-line notice and no behavioral drift.
Parity test proves identical deposit state/output vs directive update on a vendored install.
No regression to #2053 version resolution or #2055/#2056 refresh transaction.
UPGRADING.md + doctor prose name the single canonical verb; CHANGELOG updated.
